business_scope.primary_industry_name: Blank-Check Entity for Public Market Acquisition Mergers (SPAC)

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada–European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Canada–United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement (Canada–UK TCA)
Canada–United States Tax Convention (1980, as amended by Protocols)

C-46, Part II.1 (s. 462.31); Beneficial Ownership Transparency Act, S.B.C. 2023, c. 15, ss. 2–14; Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57, ss. 9–13, 22–26, Part 10.1; Business Corporations Regulation, B.C. Reg. 198/2004.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Status for each corporate member or direct shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official companies registry in the foreign shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for states party to the 1961 Hague Convention) or Consular Legalization for non-member states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copy and proof of residential address of each proposed individual director, officer, and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public / commissioner for taking affidavits in the individual's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial ownership structure chart and declaration, certified by each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary of the immediate shareholder / notary public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Legal opinion letter on the validity and ownership of the ultimate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Outside counsel in the parent entity's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, if the opinion is to be relied upon in BC proceedings

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank letter of reference or proof of maintainability of escrow account funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corresponding bank for the Trust_Escrow_Account / professional bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized and apostilled / consularized according to bank's KYC policy

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, and UBOs against FinTRAC PEP, OFAC, UN Security Council consolidated lists, UK HMT sanctions, and Canadian sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act (S.C. 1992, c. 17), the United Nations Act (R.S.C. 1985, c. U-2), and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (S.C. 2017, c. 21); enhanced due diligence is required for PEPs, close associates, and higher-risk jurisdictions, including source-of-wealth verification and ongoing transaction monitoring. For SPAC activities, BC Securities Commission (BCSC) registration/relief and CIRO / dealer requirements must be assessed for securities-law triggers.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Corporate Online (Corporate Registry, Service BC)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A BC corporate name must be in English or French characters; Roman-letter words are accepted, and non-Latin script terms must be transliterated or translated into English or French. The name must include a distinctive element plus a corporate designation ('Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.' or 'Limited') and must not be misleading. Numeric names are permitted where the name is merely a number identified in the incorporation notice.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 28 days of a name refusal, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration request to the BC Registrar of Companies via BC Corporate Online or by letter to the Corporate Registry (PO Box 9431 Stn Prov Govt, Victoria, BC V8W 9V3), attaching the notice of refusal, statutory grounds for reconsideration, and any consents from the ministry or regulatory body whose approval is required for a sensitive token. The Registrar must render a revised decision after considering public interest. If the reconsideration fails, the applicant may either file a new name reservation with a different distinctive element or apply to the Supreme Court of British Columbia for judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 209. A name reservation may not be extended beyond its validity period; a new fee must be paid.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for the statutory registered office; BCBCA s. 22 requires a physical street address in British Columbia where the registrar may serve documents and company records are kept. A virtual office may be used solely as a business or mailing address, provided the registered office and records office are at a physical BC location used during normal business hours.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 25% within 12 months for a SPAC structured as a non-disclosing, medium-risk reporting issuer; higher (35%) if securities distribution is made to retail BC investors, FinTRAC reports suspicious transactions, or BCSC files a compliance review.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (British Columbia), S.B.C. 2002, c. 57, as amended (BCBCA); applicable sections include s. 10 (incorporation application), s. 11 (certificate of incorporation), s. 43 (notice of articles), s. 51 (records), s. 114 (at least one director), s. 173-187 (share structure and share issuance); for the SPAC public offering, also the Securities Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 418, and National Instrument 41-101 as applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Ministry of Citizens' Services, Province of British Columbia - Registrar of Companies, Victoria Corporate Registry Office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application (Form 1), Notice of Articles (Form 2), and Articles, filed electronically through BC Corporate Online, resulting in the Registrar-issued Certificate of Incorporation (online filing fee CAD $350; approximate USD equivalent $285).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required under the BCBCA; authorized share capital is set at the incorporators' discretion. For this SPAC, aggregate gross proceeds from the initial public offering must be deposited into a segregated trust/escrow account maintained by a Canadian chartered bank or licensed trust company, released only for permitted interest, qualifying acquisition completion, or shareholder redemption, per the final prospectus, NI 41-101, and TSXV Policy 2.4 escrow rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation accepts the subscription of [Subscriber] for 1,000,000 Common Shares at CAD $0.50 per share, issues such shares fully paid and non-assessable, and deposits the proceeds into the corporate bank account to be held pending establishment of the trust escrow. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at Suite 100, 1234 West Georgia Street, Vancouver, British Columbia, and that [Agent Name] is appointed as registered office representative under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia). RESOLVED, that [Name A] be appointed President and Chief Executive Officer, [Name B] be appointed Corporate Secretary, and [Name C] be appointed Chief Financial Officer, each to serve until the next annual general meeting or until successors are duly elected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services - BC Corporate Online Name Request Portal (Registrar of Companies)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a Name Reservation Request through BC Corporate Online, providing up to three proposed corporate names in priority order (e.g., 'XYZ Capital Corp.'). The name must be distinct, not prohibitive, and compliant with the Business Corporations Act Name Regulation. Pay the CAD $30 name request fee online and obtain the 56-day name reservation number.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, promptly file a revised name reservation request without prejudice; a reconsideration request may be submitted to the Registrar of Companies if the applicant believes the refusal is factually erroneous.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Incorporation Application and Governance Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel acting on behalf of the incorporator; subsequent filing through BC Corporate Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Form 1 Incorporation Application, Form 2 Notice of Articles, and the Corporation's Articles. Define the authorized share structure (unlimited common shares, unlimited first preferred shares issuable in series, and SPAC-specific special rights). Propose one or more first directors and obtain each director's signed Consent to Act, designate the BC registered office address and registered office representative, and specify the first financial year end.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation (custom or BC standard Form 10)
Signed Consent to Act as Director for each first director
Registered office address and office representative consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Incomplete drafts are corrected by counsel and resubmitted; the incorporation filing queue on BC Corporate Online allows editing prior to payment and submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission, Fee Payment and Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Ministry of Citizens' Services, Victoria - Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Form 1, Form 2, and Articles through BC Corporate Online; pay the CAD $350 incorporation fee, plus any applicable priority processing fee, by accepted electronic payment method. Upon registration, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation under the Registrar's seal. Download and retain the certificate, updated Notice of Articles, and the company's BC registry number.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is requisitioned, respond to the requisition within 21 days with requested particulars or amendments; a rejected application is refunded and may be re-filed after correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Board Meeting and First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation (internal corporate governance; no registry filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first organizational meeting of the board (or pass a unanimous written resolution signed by all directors) adopting the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution: accept share subscriptions, issue fully paid shares to founders/subscribers, establish the registered office and registered office representative, appoint the President/CEO, Corporate Secretary, and CFO, approve signing authorities, select a fiscal year end, and authorize the opening of bank and trust escrow accounts.
required_dossiers: Unanimous written resolution of the directors
Share subscription agreements and payment evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any director's consent is defective or signature is missing, the resolution is re-circulated and re-executed; minutes are corrected by subsequent board resolution and placed in the corporate minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Tax, Payroll and Registry Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online); WorkSafeBC; BC Ministry of Finance - Consumer Taxation Branch; BC Corporate Registry (annual report filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the federal Business Number via CRA Business Registration Online; register for the GST/HST account (nil or exempt treatment for financial supplies may apply), select a payroll deduction account if officers/staff are compensated, and register with the BC corporate registry for ongoing annual reporting. Register the employer account with WorkSafeBC to secure occupational injury coverage. If required, register the PST account with the BC Ministry of Finance (generally not required for exempt investment activities). Maintain the statutory registers (shareholders, directors, beneficial ownership, and transparency registers) at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Notice of Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or provincial registration is queried for incomplete information, amend the account profile via CRA My Business Account or BC Corporate Online; account activation dates may be backdated to incorporation upon evidence of commencement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Securities, Exchange Listing, AML and Municipal Licensing Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: British Columbia Securities Commission (BCSC); TSX Venture Exchange (TSXV) Listings Division; Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC); municipal business licensing office of the city of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a preliminary prospectus with the BCSC under NI 41-101 and obtain a receipt, then file the final prospectus; secure conditional and final listing approval from TSXV (or an exchange recognized by the BCSC) for the SPAC's common shares; execute a trust escrow agreement with a Canadian Schedule I bank or licensed trust company to hold gross offering proceeds; implement the AML/CTF compliance program applicable to the escrow/trust arrangements and sponsor, making required registrations with FINTRAC if the SPAC or sponsor conducts money-transmitting services; obtain the municipal business licence for the registered premises, comply with BC Fire Code and the BC Building Code occupancy requirements, and register with WorkSafeBC for the office workplace.
required_dossiers: Audited opening financial statements or balance sheet
Trust escrow agreement with bank/trust company
TSXV listing application and sponsor lock-up agreement
Fire safety and BC Building Code occupancy certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to BCSC comment letters within 10 business days and amend the prospectus accordingly; appeal any TSXV listing refusal through the Listings Committee; for municipal licence or fire safety deficiencies, complete the corrective notices and re-inspection, with temporary occupancy continued under a permit if allowed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: British Columbia Securities Commission (BCSC) - Corporate Finance Division and TSX Venture Exchange (TSXV) Listings Division; City of Vancouver (or the city of the registered office) Business Licence Office; WorkSafeBC - Occupational Health and Safety Division
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: SPAC Qualification Licence Set - BCSC Final Prospectus Receipt, TSXV Listing Approval, and Municipal Business Licence for the registered office

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Assessment Office of British Columbia and the BC Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for the head-office financial vehicle; a full environmental impact assessment under the Environmental Assessment Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 43, is triggered only if the SPAC's qualifying acquisition brings a designated physical project into British Columbia.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: The SPAC's own office operations have no direct discharges, but any acquired target must demonstrate compliance with the BC Environmental Management Act, S.B.C. 2003, c. 53, including Waste Discharge Regulation permits for air/land/water discharges, Municipal Wastewater Regulation effluent limits, VOC and odour limits under applicable BC air quality objectives, Contaminated Sites Regulation obligations, and hazardous waste handling under the federal Transportation of Dangerous Goods Act and BC regulation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and BC Fire Code compliance certificate for the registered office premises; structural load and occupancy verification under the BC Building Code; WorkSafeBC clearances for office ergonomics/safety, first aid, and employer registration; landlord-issued confirmation of fire alarm, sprinklers, and building emergency plans.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) is the federal tax administration; registration and filings are processed through Business Registration Online (BRO) and My Business Account portal. The British Columbia Ministry of Finance administers provincial sales tax (PST), employer health tax, and BC corporate registration via Corporate Online and eTaxBC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign SPAC must obtain a Canadian federal Business Number (BN) through CRA Business Registration Online using Form RC1 or RC1A. A GST/HST program account should be opened when taxable supplies exceed C$30,000 in any single calendar quarter or over four consecutive calendar quarters. Voluntary GST/HST registration is advisable before closing acquisition transactions. The foreign corporation must submit its certified constitutional documents, foreign registration details, a BC registered office address, and a resident BC agent for service. Federal incorporation through Corporations Canada produces a number integrated with CRA accounts; provincially incorporated BC corporations receive a BC incorporation number linked to the federal BN. Separate CRA program accounts for payroll and indirect tax remittances must be created as activities commence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide U.S.-style check-the-box or pass-through elections for a business corporation. A Canadian-resident SPAC is taxed at entity level on worldwide income. Available elections include the section 216 election for non-residents to compute Canadian-source net income on a net basis; subsection 217 election for non-resident employees; associate election under section 156 of the Excise Tax Act to treat closely related GST/HST registrants as one registrant; and the section 21 election to capitalize interest and foreign exchange costs on acquisition debt. Hybrid mismatch rules in the Income Tax Act are mandatory and documentation-driven rather than elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal VAT-style tax) plus British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST, retail sales/use tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies, other than exempt supplies, over four consecutive calendar quarters or in one calendar quarter; separate BC PST registration is required for vendors making taxable sales in BC, with applicable small-seller exemptions only for limited out-of-province sellers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not currently mandate country-wide real-time fiscal clearance, digital tax stamping, or continuous transaction control (CTC) e-invoicing. CRA accepts electronic invoices meeting standard readability and integrity requirements. GST/HST registrants above threshold must file and remit electronically using GST/HST NETFILE, XML, or CRA-supported API channels. BC PST returns are submitted electronically through eTaxBC. No pre-clearance or government-controlled e-invoicing repository exists.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada by the supplier qualify for zero-rating under section 1 of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act if the supplier possesses documentary evidence of export and delivery occurs outside Canada. Services performed directly to non-residents and related to exported goods, or performed wholly outside Canada, may also be zero-rated where the conditions of Schedule VI are met. For BC PST, deliveries of tangible goods shipped directly out of BC to foreign destinations are generally exempt from PST with fully documented proof of export. SPAC financial and trust-related services normally fall within exempt financial services rather than zero-rated supplies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canada Border Services Agency Form A6 or B13A) filed through the Canadian Export Reporting System
Bill of Lading, air waybill, or cargo receipt evidencing physical delivery to the non-resident consignee
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/wire/FX settlement confirmation evidencing receipt of export proceeds from the foreign purchaser
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess beyond the normal four-year period where misrepresentation or fraud is established. Claiming zero-rating without adequate export evidence results in denial and clawback of input tax credits and refunds, gross-negligence penalties of 20% of the claimed amounts, false-statement penalties under section 280.1 of the Excise Tax Act, and interest accrual. Criminal prosecution for wilful tax evasion can impose fines up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to five years. BC PST audits similarly may reassess, deny exemption claims, and apply prescribed interest and civil penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as monetary authority under the Bank of Canada Act; Canada maintains a free-floating exchange-rate regime with no dedicated foreign-exchange control agency. OSFI (Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions) supervises all federally chartered banks and trust companies; FINTRAC administers cross-border transaction monitoring and reporting under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) and associated regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility applies to both capital and current account items for residents and non-residents. No Bank of Canada or Department of Finance authorization is required for inbound SPAC IPO subscription remittances, escrow deposits, redemption payments, or business-combination disbursements. Profit and capital repatriation is unfettered, subject only to Part XIII non-resident withholding tax (statutory 25%, typically reduced under tax treaty, on dividends and certain interest to non-residents) and to information reporting obligations to the Canada Revenue Agency ('CRA') (e.g., Form T1135 for specified foreign property and Form T1134 for foreign affiliates, where triggered). The SPAC may hold escrow proceeds in USD, CAD, or any freely convertible currency without restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory surrender, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation deadline for export proceeds or any cross-border receipts, including IPO and escrow inflow. Funds may remain offshore or onshore indefinitely in any currency. The only compliance hooks are transparency requirements: FINTRAC mandatory reporting of electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more, CRA information returns for foreign property/affiliates, and FATCA/CRS account reporting by the financial institution. No approval or declaration to the Bank of Canada is required at any time.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for capital escrow and trust custody; MEDIUM for ancillary operational payments. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer, etc.) are not authorized deposit-taking institutions in Canada and cannot act as custodian or escrow holder for SPAC IPO proceeds under the Trust and Loan Companies Act (Canada) or BC Financial Institutions Act. They may provide limited transactional services (FX conversion, payroll and vendor payments) only if registered or exempt under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) transitional regime, and any use must be supplemental to, not a replacement for, an OSFI-regulated bank or trust company clearing rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory mandate for physical branch attendance exists under PCMLTFA; however, banks impose enhanced due diligence for medium-risk SPAC vehicles. Remote onboarding is permitted for Canadian-resident directors using live video verification, credit-bureau authentication, and electronic signature. Non-resident directors, sponsors, or beneficial owners from non-common-law or higher-risk jurisdictions are commonly required to appear in person at a Canadian branch or at a qualified correspondent bank, or to deliver an apostilled/notarized identity and authority package together with a banker's confirmation letter from a regulated institution. A structured interview with corporate banking and AML compliance officers is mandatory in all practical scenarios.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex offshore beneficial-ownership structure (Cayman/BVI holding layers, nominee shareholders, or discretionary trusts above the SPAC)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified ownership chain from ultimate individual beneficial owners through each intermediary; CRS/FATCA self-certifications (Canada Form RC518); certificates of good standing for each entity; legal opinion from Canadian and offshore counsel confirming economic substance, absence of bearer shares, and legitimacy of trust/nominee arrangements; audited financial statements or opening balance-sheet pack; sponsor and promoter biographies with independent professional references.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bulk inbound subscription wires from multiple unrelated subscribers lacking commercial or trade underlying documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed subscription agreements per subscriber; final prospectus or offering memorandum receipted by the British Columbia Securities Commission (BCSC) or Canadian Securities Administrators; escrow agreement among the SPAC, bank, and qualified custodian/trustee; board resolutions authorizing share issuance and escrow deposit instructions; SWIFT MT103 payment trail with subscriber identification for all material positions; transfer-agent allocation schedule.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Escrow release and redemption payments to non-resident shareholders following business-combination announcement or shareholder vote
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed business-combination agreement; shareholder redemption notices and redemption register; board minutes approving continuation, amalgamation, or dissolution; Part XIII withholding calculation and CRA remittance advice (proprietary or NR4 forms); fund-flow statement mapping escrow release to lawful consideration; target-company valuation and fairness opinion; shareholder residence and nexus-status declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically exposed persons (PEPs) or sanctioned-jurisdiction nationals among sponsors, directors, or 10%+ shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank-prescribed PEP declarations from each relevant individual; independent enhanced due diligence report from an internationally recognized screening provider; negative sanction-list findings across OSFI, OFAC, UN and EU lists; independent director oversight framework with documented enhanced monitoring procedures; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds reports supported by bank statements, tax returns, and asset-ownership evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent transactional patterns between operating account and escrow account flagged during periodic transaction monitoring
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Adopted treasury policy with mandatory segregation schedule; monthly reconciliation between escrow trust balance, operating ledger, CRA filings, and audited financial statements; expense-support package comprising vendor agreements, itemized invoices, wire-transfer forms with descriptive purpose codes; independent auditor's management letter confirming control environment and absence of commingling.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: IPO subscription proceeds are routed via SWIFT MT103 through the Canadian bank's correspondent network into the dedicated SPAC escrow account held with an OSFI-regulated bank or trust company. Field 70 (Remittance Information) must carry a descriptive narrative such as 'SPAC [ticker] IPO subscription – escrow per prospectus dated [date]'; field 50K ordering party must match the subscriber in the final allocation schedule. The bank places funds in 'pending verification' status until the transfer agent's share-allocation certificate is delivered. USD subscriptions clear via bank-internal US dollar clearing facilities (e.g., Fedwire through a US affiliate or correspondent); CAD conversions, where elected, are executed at bank-published spot with no governmental approval. Over-subscription refunds are returned via MT103 RE referencing the original message to prevent layering alerts. All receipts are subject to criminal-record and sanction screening at the institution level.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails structure: (a) Shareholder redemptions and liquidation distributions — SWIFT MT103 over Fedwire/CHIPS for USD and LVTS (Large Value Transfer System) for CAD, with narrative 'SPAC redemption per [date] meeting', pre-funded through the escrow account; Part XIII withholding remitted to CRA with NR4 filings where applicable; (b) Business-combination purchase price — SWIFT MT103 with supporting board-pack transmission, or standby/commercial letter of credit (UCP600) issued by the Canadian bank and advised/confirmed by the target-side bank for deferred or earn-out consideration; (c) Operating disbursements — domestic CAD rails comprising LVTS wires, ACSS (Automated Clearing Settlement System) for ACH/cheques, and corporate payment cards; (d) Routine USD obligations — internal cross-border sweep to the bank's US correspondent for same-day Fedwire settlement. Each outbound wire must be matched to an approved payment matrix and, for escrow releases, to a signed board resolution and reason code.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot foreign-exchange contracts (CAD/USD and major crosses) with OSFI-regulated counterparties for immediate conversion of escrow or operational funds
Plain-vanilla deliverable over-the-counter (OTC) currency forwards with tenors aligned to the anticipated acquisition closing or redemption date
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) where onshore deliverable liquidity is unavailable; legally permissible under Canadian law but generally unnecessary for the CAD/USD pair
Cross-currency swaps (fixed-floating and floating-floating) executed pursuant to an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a Canadian law Schedule and appropriate credit support annex
Vanilla OTC call and put currency options for hedging redemption-value and purchase-price uncertainty with limited premium risk
Exchange-traded currency futures and options traded on CME or TMX (Montreal Exchange) with margin collateralized by escrow-grade government securities

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report under the Business Corporations Act (SBC 2002, c. 57), certifying current directors, registered office and records office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia (BC Corporate Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months after each anniversary of the date of incorporation; if the vehicle is a CBCA federal corporation, the Corporations Canada annual return is due within 60 days of the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 100 per delinquent year; failure to file an annual report for 2 consecutive years authorizes the BC Registrar to administratively strike off (dissolve) the company; certificates of good standing and certain registry searches are blocked until cured

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal return with the integrated BC provincial corporate income tax component)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); BC Ministry of Finance provincial component administered through the T2 system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of each fiscal year (Income Tax Act, s. 150(1)); balance of tax due generally 2 months after year-end for non-CCPC issuers, with instalments as required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per complete month (maximum 12 months); repeat offender rate of 10% plus 2% per month (maximum 20 months); daily compound interest; arbitrary assessment and loss of carry-back relief under the Income Tax Act if filing is delayed

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual continuous disclosure package for a reporting issuer SPAC: audited annual financial statements, management discussion and analysis, CEO/CFO certificates and annual information form (if applicable), filed on SEDAR+
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: British Columbia Securities Commission (BCSC) through SEDAR+ (CSA electronic filing system)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after fiscal year-end for non-venture reporting issuers; venture issuers are allowed 120 days (National Instrument 51-102)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Issuer default alert and late filing fees under the securities fee rules; cease trade order risk; loss of short-form prospectus and resale exemption eligibility; BCSC administrative penalty and enforcement proceedings for material non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM): notice of meeting, presentation of annual (audited) financial statements, election or re-election of directors, appointment of auditor, and execution of meeting minutes (non-reporting private companies may use a unanimous written resolution where permitted under the BCBCA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate minute book at the registered office; oversight and enforcement by BC Registries and Online Services; reporting issuers also subject to BCSC proxy and continuous disclosure rules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once in each calendar year and no more than 15 months after the previous annual general meeting (BCBCA, s. 182)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Any member or director may apply to the BC Supreme Court for an order compelling the meeting; persistent non-compliance may support BC Registries compliance action and, for reporting issuers, BCSC enforcement proceedings including cease trade orders

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% combined (15% federal Part I + 12% British Columbia general corporate rate)
